messages:
maya: Nightdash just fired an alert — batch-window tail latency +32% for service runtime-infer after merge of PR #5821 (canary). https://dash.redwood/runtime-infer :warning:

liam: saw it. CI perf job failed for that merge: https://ci.redwood/12345/jobs/6789 — flaky? but numbers look real.

deploy-bot: Canary health check failing on canary-3: 5/10 unhealthy instances (latency)

sophia: quick look at kernel-selection logs on canary-3 — lots of fallbacks to kernel "stream-kv-compact" at seq_len ~1024. That shouldn't be primary for these requests.

akshay: flagged PR #5821 changed adaptive batching thresholds (max_batch_wait_ms 8 -> 20) and a small tweak in the scheduler's windowing. Could explain larger queues + different kernel choices.

jordan: KV cache metrics look off too — replica-1 miss rate jumped from 4% -> 13% around the merge timestamp. Maybe batch expansion is pushing more unique prefixes and evicting hot keys.

maya: can someone run the local batch sim and a quick profile? `python tools/bench/batch_sim.py --profile --model gpt-small --seed 42`

liam: running now, will paste p99/p50.

liam: sim results (snippet):
```
baseline (main before PR): p50=22ms p95=68ms p99=85ms
canary (with PR): p50=28ms p95=95ms p99=130ms
```

sophia: Oof. 99th jumped a lot. Starting a git bisect locally to narrow commits between scheduler tweak and kernel selector tweak.

akshay: I started bisect on our perf harness. suspect interaction between commit `4f3b9c` (batching window change) and `a9d2e1` (kernel selector heuristic). Either alone maybe OK, together bad.

jordan: logs from runtime on canary-3 around the spike:
```
[2026-03-17T02:13:40Z] batch_queue: window_expand to 128 (wait_ms=20)
[2026-03-17T02:13:40Z] kernel_selector: prefer kernel stream-kv-compact (fallback true)
[2026-03-17T02:13:41Z] kv_cache: evict prefix user:abc:chunk: 14 entries
[2026-03-17T02:13:41Z] request: id=... latency=189ms p99
```

maya: pretty convincing. Two-pronged effect: larger wait -> larger batches -> different kernel chosen -> more KV churn -> evictions -> more cold prefixes -> higher tail.

liam: bisect result: reverting `4f3b9c` (batching wait change) alone brings p99 back to ~88ms in the harness. Kernel selector heuristic change less impactful in isolation.

akshay: I recommend reverting the scheduler change from canary immediately and keep kernel selector tweak in the queue for more testing. Will open revert PR.

maya: please go ahead. Also add a regression test in perf CI to simulate prefix-hotset + expanded batches.

deploy-bot: Revert PR #5839 (revert batching-window change) merged to release/canary by akshay. Canary redeploy started.

jordan: after revert rollout, tail reduced: Nightdash shows +4% vs baseline now. KV miss rate back to ~5%.

maya: great. Leave canary pinned on the reverted release for 24h and follow-up with a postmortem and a perf regression test.

sophia: I'll draft the PM with timeline, bisect commands, and suggested test harness inputs.

liam: adding perf regression alert in CI to run batch_sim with hot-prefix pattern nightly.

maya: thanks all. :thumbsup: We'll close if overnight looks clean.

jordan: note for postmortem — consider adding a canary-only kernel selector override flag to isolate future rollout experiments.

maya: agreed. I'll add to action items.

liam: any objections to marking this as resolved for tonight?

akshay: no objections. monitoring on.

deploy-bot: Canary health check OK on 6/6 instances.

maya: closing for now, will publish short incident summary tomorrow.

sophia: thanks, good catch everyone.
